title: Unit – 3 : Session – 1 : SLO – 2 | Multithreading vs Multitasking
sections: Fill: Multithreading involves multiple THREADS running within a single process.
T/F: Multitasking refers to a system running multiple processes simultaneously. — TRUE
MCQ: Best represents multitasking → B) Running a web browser and a text editor at the same time
Fill: In multitasking, each PROCESS has its own memory space.
T/F: Multithreading consumes more system resources compared to multitasking. — FALSE (threads share memory and are lighter)
MCQ: Generally faster in terms of context switching → A) Multithreading
Fill: Multithreading is useful for tasks that need to run CONCURRENTLY (in parallel) within the same application.
T/F: In multitasking, processes are isolated from each other. — TRUE
MCQ: Typically shares memory space between its units → A) Multithreading
Fill: Multitasking is often managed by the OPERATING SYSTEM (OS).
